snp2.8:1.1:
Because:
When you honor
—as the devas, Indra—
one from whom
you might learn the Dhamma,
snp2.8:1.3:
he, learned, honored,
confident in you,
shows you the Dhamma.
snp2.8:2.1:
You, enlightened, heedful,
befriending a teacher like that,
snp2.8:2.2:
practicing the Dhamma
in line with the Dhamma,
pondering,
giving it priority,
snp2.8:3.1: But if you consort with a piddling fool
snp2.8:3.2:
who’s envious,
hasn’t come to the goal,
snp2.8:3.3:
you’ll go to death
without
having cleared up
the Dhamma right here,
with
your doubts unresolved.
snp2.8:4.1: Like a man gone down to a river—
snp2.8:4.3: and swept away in the current:
snp2.8:4.4: How can he help others across?
snp2.8:5.1:
Even so:
He who hasn’t
cleared up the Dhamma,
snp2.8:5.2:
attended to the meaning
of what the learned say,
snp2.8:5.4:
How can he get others
to comprehend?
snp2.8:6.1:
But as one who’s embarked
on a sturdy boat,
snp2.8:6.3:
would—thoughtful, skillful,
knowing the needed techniques—
carry many others across,
snp2.8:7.3: can get other people to comprehend—
snp2.8:7.4:
when the conditions have arisen
for them to lend ear.
snp2.8:8.1:
So:
You should befriend
a person of integrity—
snp2.8:8.3:
Practicing so
as to know the goal,
snp2.8:8.4:
when you’ve experienced the Dhamma,
you get bliss.
